name: FREE SAMPLE · RSS to LinkedIn Draft (from The Content Engine)

parameters.content:
## FREE SAMPLE · RSS to LinkedIn Draft
Watches your blog's RSS feed. For each new post, AI writes one LinkedIn post draft using only that post's facts, and saves it to a Google Sheet queue. Nothing is posted; you copy, edit and post it yourself.

Setup: put your feed URL in New Post. Make a Sheet with a tab named Queue and headers: date, title, url, draft, status. Paste the Sheet ID in Config.

**Credentials:** open each node with a red warning and pick or create your own Gmail OAuth2, Google Sheets OAuth2 and OpenAI credentials. Nothing is hard-coded. Test with your own address before you activate.

assignments.name: STYLE
assignments.value: Plain, specific, first person, short paragraphs.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ {"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "temperature": 0.2, "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "Write one LinkedIn post (120-200 words) from this blog post in the style given. Strong first line, short paragraphs, end with a question, put the URL on the last line. Use only facts in the text; never invent numbers or quotes. Reply as JSON: {\"draft\":string}."}, {"role": "user", "content": JSON.stringify({ style: $('Config').first().json.STYLE, title: $('New Post').item.json.title, url: $('New Post').item.json.link, text: ($('New Post').item.json.contentSnippet || '').slice(0, 8000) })}], "response_format": {"type": "json_object"}} }}

parameters.jsCode:
// Skip posts where the AI reply could not be parsed; they are not queued as junk rows
return $input.all().map((it, i) => { let d = ''; try { d = JSON.parse(it.json.choices[0].message.content).draft; } catch (e) { d = ''; } const p = $('New Post').all()[i].json; return { json: { title: p.title, url: p.link, draft: d } }; }).filter(i => i.json.draft);
